The invention relates to a field-sequential color image display device designed to reduce color breakup while maintaining a wide color reproduction range. In a field-sequential display system, red, green, and blue light are emitted in separate frame periods, and the displayed color image is produced by rapidly switching these light sources in synchronization with image modulation. Although this method can provide high color performance without using color filters, it may cause color breakup when the viewer’s eyes move or when objects in the image move. The invention addresses this issue while preserving the display’s ability to reproduce a broad range of colors.

The device is also configured to improve the transparency of a transparent display area within the displayed image. This is particularly useful for displays that include see-through regions, such as transparent displays, head-up displays, or augmented-reality display devices. In such applications, it is important not only to display vivid color images but also to allow background scenery or objects behind the display to be clearly visible through selected regions of the screen.

To achieve these functions, the device includes a light source data computation portion. This portion generates drive light source data by modifying initial light source data. The modification is performed based on a target transparent color, which represents the desired color appearance of the transparent area, and a target color display area proportion, which indicates the intended proportion of the display area used for color image display. By taking these parameters into account, the computation portion determines suitable driving conditions for the light sources so that the display can balance color reproduction, transparency, and suppression of color breakup.

The display further includes a light source driver that drives red, green, and blue LEDs. These LEDs are operated during their respective frame periods in accordance with the drive light source data computed by the light source data computation portion. By controlling the light emission intensity or timing of each LED for the red, green, and blue frame periods, the display can reproduce the intended color image while reducing visual artifacts associated with field-sequential operation.

In addition, a spatial light modulation drive portion controls the liquid crystal transmittance of each pixel. This control is performed so as to maximize the transparency of the transparent display area. In other words, for pixels belonging to the transparent region, the liquid crystal modulation is adjusted to allow as much external light as possible to pass through the display while still maintaining the intended appearance of the image. As a result, the invention provides a display device capable of suppressing color breakup, preserving color reproduction performance, and enhancing transparency in designated transparent areas of the displayed image.
outputs.L4:
A field-sequential transparent liquid crystal display device and a method for driving the same are provided. The device receives input image data and analyzes the image to determine a target transparent color and a proportion of transparent areas included in the displayed image. Based on this information, the device adjusts drive data supplied to red, green, and blue light-emitting diodes used as field-sequential light sources. The adjustment is performed so that light transmission through transparent portions of the display is increased, thereby improving the visibility of objects or backgrounds located behind the transparent display.

In operation, the transparent liquid crystal display sequentially emits red, green, and blue light during different time periods while controlling the transmittance of liquid crystal pixels in synchronization with the emitted colors. When the input image contains a large transparent area, the drive levels of the RGB light sources and the pixel transmittance values are controlled to allow more light to pass through those transparent regions. At the same time, the device limits excessive modification of the RGB light-source balance so as to suppress color breakup, which may occur in field-sequential displays, and to prevent a substantial reduction in the displayable color gamut.

The device may calculate an optimized light-source driving condition by considering both the desired transparent appearance and the color reproduction requirements of non-transparent image regions. For example, if increasing the luminance of a particular color light source would improve transparency but would noticeably distort image colors, the system may compensate by adjusting the transmittance of corresponding pixels or by limiting the amount of light-source correction. In this way, the display can achieve a balance between enhanced transparency and stable color performance.

By controlling the RGB LED drive data together with the liquid crystal pixel transmittance, the invention maximizes the amount of light passing through transparent areas while maintaining acceptable reproduction of image colors in opaque or semi-transparent areas. As a result, the transparent display provides improved background visibility and a clearer transparent effect without significantly degrading image quality, color gamut, or viewer comfort. This makes the technology suitable for transparent televisions, showcase displays, vehicle windows, augmented-reality panels, and other applications requiring both display functionality and high see-through visibility.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for a transparent field-sequential liquid crystal display device that reduces color breakup while increasing transparency in transparent display regions.
counterfactuals.output: A transparent field-sequential liquid crystal display device includes a liquid crystal display panel having a plurality of pixels disposed in a display region including transparent display regions, a backlight unit configured to sequentially emit light of different colors, and a controller configured to drive the liquid crystal display panel in synchronization with the sequential emission of the different colors. Each pixel includes a plurality of sub-regions including a transmissive display sub-region and a transparent sub-region, wherein the transparent sub-region is configured to transmit external light to increase transparency of the transparent display region. The controller drives the pixels according to a field-sequential driving scheme in which color image data is temporally divided into a plurality of color fields, and controls at least one of a light emission period, a liquid crystal response period, a pixel charging period, and gray-level data supplied to the pixels to reduce color breakup caused by temporal separation of the color fields. Accordingly, the display device provides improved see-through visibility while suppressing color breakup in moving images.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a technical summary of an invention involving RGB LED field-sequential driving, liquid crystal spatial light modulation, and adjustment of light source data based on target transparent colors.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention relates to a display or illumination apparatus that produces color images using field-sequential RGB light emission in combination with a liquid crystal spatial light modulator. The system includes red, green, and blue LED light sources, a liquid crystal panel or other spatial light modulation element, and a controller that synchronizes light-source driving with modulation of the liquid crystal layer.

In operation, one image frame is divided into a plurality of color sub-fields corresponding to the RGB LEDs. During each sub-field, one or more LEDs are driven to emit light of a selected color component, while the liquid crystal spatial light modulator is controlled to set pixel-by-pixel transmittance values corresponding to that color component. By rapidly repeating the red, green, and blue sub-fields, the observer perceives a full-color image without requiring separate color filters for each pixel.

A key feature of the invention is that the light-source drive data is not fixed solely according to nominal RGB image values. Instead, the apparatus adjusts the LED driving data based on a target transparent color or desired transmission color state. The controller determines the intended transparent color appearance for each region or pixel and modifies the RGB LED emission intensities, timings, duty ratios, or pulse widths accordingly. The liquid crystal modulation data may also be coordinated with the adjusted light-source data so that the final light transmitted through the liquid crystal panel matches the desired chromaticity, brightness, and transparency characteristics.

This adjustment can compensate for spectral characteristics of the LEDs, wavelength-dependent transmittance of the liquid crystal panel, optical losses, color mixing behavior, and variations caused by the transparent or semi-transparent nature of the display. For example, when a target transparent color requires a specific balance of red, green, and blue transmission, the controller may increase or decrease the drive level of one or more LEDs and alter the corresponding liquid crystal gray levels to achieve the desired perceived color while maintaining luminance and contrast.

The invention can improve color reproducibility, reduce color shift, and enhance image quality in field-sequential liquid crystal displays, transparent displays, optical shutters, augmented-reality panels, and other systems where controllable colored light is transmitted through a liquid crystal spatial light modulator. It also enables efficient LED usage by allocating light output according to the desired transparent color instead of relying only on conventional pixel RGB values.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: In patent language, describe an invention for a transparent LCD using red, green, and blue LEDs driven per frame and pixel-level liquid crystal transmittance control to inhibit color breakup.
counterfactuals.output:
**Title:** Transparent Liquid Crystal Display With Frame-Sequential Light Emitting Diode Illumination and Pixel-Level Transmittance Control for Inhibiting Color Breakup

**Abstract**

A transparent liquid crystal display apparatus is disclosed. The apparatus includes a transparent liquid crystal display panel having a plurality of pixels, a transparent or edge-coupled illumination unit including red, green, and blue light emitting diodes, and a controller configured to drive the red, green, and blue light emitting diodes in synchronization with image frames. For each frame, the controller determines pixel-level liquid crystal transmittance values corresponding to respective red, green, and blue image components and controls the liquid crystal display panel to selectively transmit light emitted by the red, green, and blue light emitting diodes. The controller coordinates the timing and intensity of the light emitting diodes with the response of the liquid crystal pixels so that color components are presented in a temporally compensated manner. By controlling pixel transmittance at the frame or sub-frame level and by synchronizing such control with the sequential driving of the red, green, and blue light emitting diodes, perceived color breakup is inhibited while maintaining transparency of the display.

**Detailed Description**

An embodiment of the invention provides a transparent liquid crystal display device including a liquid crystal display panel configured to transmit ambient background light when in a transparent state. The panel may include first and second transparent substrates, transparent electrodes disposed on the substrates, a liquid crystal layer interposed between the substrates, and a plurality of individually addressable pixels. Each pixel is controllable to assume a selected optical transmittance in response to an applied pixel voltage.

The display further includes an illumination assembly comprising a plurality of light emitting diodes including red light emitting diodes, green light emitting diodes, and blue light emitting diodes. The light emitting diodes may be arranged along one or more edges of a transparent light guide, integrated into a transparent backlight structure, or otherwise optically coupled to the liquid crystal panel so as to provide colored illumination through the panel without substantially impairing see-through visibility.

A display controller receives image data including red, green, and blue color components for pixels of a frame. The controller generates, for each frame, liquid crystal drive signals for the pixels and light source drive signals for the red, green, and blue light emitting diodes. In one embodiment, the red, green, and blue light emitting diodes are driven sequentially during respective time periods associated with a frame. During a red emission period, pixel transmittance values are set according to red component data; during a green emission period, pixel transmittance values are set according to green component data; and during a blue emission period, pixel transmittance values are set according to blue component data.

To inhibit color breakup resulting from temporal separation of the red, green, and blue illumination periods, the controller is configured to coordinate the light emitting diode drive timing with the liquid crystal response characteristics of the pixels. In particular, the controller may begin changing a pixel transmittance state before, during, or after a corresponding light emitting diode emission interval in accordance with a predetermined response compensation profile. The profile may account for liquid crystal rise time, fall time, gray-to-gray transition behavior, temperature, frame rate, or detected motion in the image.

In some embodiments, the controller subdivides a frame into a plurality of sub-frames and drives at least one of the red, green, and blue light emitting diodes more than once within a frame. Pixel transmittance values may be updated for each sub-frame, thereby reducing the temporal displacement between color components perceived by a viewer. The controller may also reduce color breakup by adjusting the relative emission durations, emission intensities, or emission order of the red, green, and blue light emitting diodes based on image content or motion information.

In further embodiments, the controller performs pixel-level color breakup compensation. For a pixel or group of pixels, the controller determines whether image motion, high contrast, or saturated color content is likely to produce visible color breakup. When such a condition is detected, the controller modifies at least one of: a liquid crystal transmittance value, an LED emission intensity, a sub-frame duration, or a temporal order of color presentation. The modification may include distributing a color component over multiple emission periods, inserting a white or mixed-color emission period, reducing peak chromatic intensity, or applying motion-compensated transmittance values to spatially or temporally align red, green, and blue perceived images.

Because the display panel is transparent, the controller may further control the liquid crystal pixels to maintain a desired see-through transmittance when image content is absent or when a transparent display mode is selected. The light emitting diodes may be dimmed or disabled during transparent operation. In an augmented display mode, the LEDs provide controlled color illumination through selected pixels while other pixels remain highly transmissive to ambient light.

**Example Claim Language**

1. A transparent display apparatus comprising:  
   a transparent liquid crystal display panel including a plurality of pixels, each pixel having an electrically controllable optical transmittance;  
   an illumination unit optically coupled to the transparent liquid crystal display panel and comprising red, green, and blue light emitting diodes; and  
   a controller configured to drive the red, green, and blue light emitting diodes during respective temporal portions of an image frame and to control, at a pixel level, transmittance of the plurality of pixels in synchronization with the respective temporal portions,  
   wherein the controller is further configured to modify at least one of pixel transmittance timing, pixel transmittance magnitude, light emitting diode emission timing, and light emitting diode emission intensity to inhibit perceptible color breakup.

2. The transparent display apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to drive the red, green, and blue light emitting diodes sequentially within each image frame.

3. The transparent display apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to determine red, green, and blue component values for each pixel and to set a transmittance of each pixel during a corresponding red, green, or blue illumination period according to the respective component value.

4. The transparent display apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to compensate for liquid crystal response delay by initiating a change in pixel transmittance before an emission period of a corresponding one of the red, green, and blue light emitting diodes.

5. The transparent display apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to divide an image frame into a plurality of sub-frames and to update pixel transmittance values for at least two of the sub-frames.

6. The transparent display apparatus of claim 5, wherein at least one of the red, green, and blue light emitting diodes is driven during more than one sub-frame of a single image frame.

7. The transparent display apparatus of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to detect motion in image data and to adjust pixel-level transmittance control based on the detected motion to reduce temporal separation of color components perceived by a viewer.

8. The transparent display apparatus of claim 1, wherein the illumination unit comprises a transparent light guide optically coupled to the red, green, and blue light emitting diodes.

9. The transparent display apparatus of claim 1, wherein the transparent liquid crystal display panel is operable in a transparent mode in which at least a portion of the plurality of pixels is controlled to maintain a high transmittance while the illumination unit is dimmed or disabled.

10. A method of operating a transparent liquid crystal display, the method comprising:  
    receiving image data including red, green, and blue component data;  
    driving red, green, and blue light emitting diodes in temporal coordination with an image frame;  
    controlling transmittance of pixels of a transparent liquid crystal display panel according to the red, green, and blue component data during corresponding temporal portions of the image frame; and  
    compensating at least one of the pixel transmittance and the light emitting diode driving to inhibit color breakup.

11. The method of claim 10, wherein compensating comprises adjusting a timing of a pixel transmittance transition based on a response characteristic of a liquid crystal material.

12. The method of claim 10, wherein compensating comprises driving at least one color of light emitting diode in multiple intervals within a single image frame.

13. The method of claim 10, wherein compensating comprises modifying pixel transmittance values in response to detected image motion.

14. The method of claim 10, wherein compensating comprises controlling emission intensity of the red, green, and blue light emitting diodes independently for each frame.

15. A non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions which, when executed by a controller of a transparent liquid crystal display, cause the controller to:  
    generate pixel-level transmittance control signals for a transparent liquid crystal panel;  
    generate red, green, and blue light emitting diode drive signals for sequential color illumination during an image frame; and  
    temporally coordinate the pixel-level transmittance control signals with the red, green, and blue light emitting diode drive signals so as to inhibit color breakup in displayed image content.
